text:
maria: Observed a fresh 95p latency spike on prod around 12:47 UTC. Perfetto trace attached shows a ~120ms idle gap between gateway send and runtime recv for several requests. Putting the trace here for quick eyeballs. :eyes:

zhang: Ugh. Is that gap CPU scheduling or PCIe / memcpy stall?

leo: Can you paste the span waterfall snippet? curious if it's waiting in client-gateway or inside runtime before kernel launch.

maria: Snippet from perfetto (filtered spans):
```
span gateway.tcp_send         [t=12345 - 12346] -> event: send on socket
span gateway.queue_dispatch   [t=12346 - 12347]
span runtime.recv_request     [t=12467 - 12468]  <-- recv happens ~120ms later
event memcpy.h2d              [t=12460 - 12462]
kernel launch conv_fwd       [t=12463 - 12464]
```
Look at the time delta between queue_dispatch and runtime.recv_request. It's the large gap, not the kernel time itself.

sophie: We pushed the batching heuristic tweak this morning (dynamic_window_ms 1->3) to reduce tiny batches. Could that introduce wait-before-send at gateway?

leo: Possibly. But the perfetto gap is inside the edge between gateway and runtime. That usually means either gateway held the request or there was backpressure on the connection / socket. Any socket retransmits?

maria: No retransmits. I correlated with nvprof/nsys capture from one of the affected nodes: infra-bot uploaded the capture and a short summary.

infra-bot: nsys capture: s3://redwood-samples/nsys/1845000000_capture.qdrep
nsys summary: kernel_launch_latency: mean=2.1ms p50=1.9ms p95=8.7ms p99=52ms; memcpy H2D spikes align with the trace gaps; PCIe TX stalled for ~30-80ms on some frames.

zhang: p99=52ms kernel launch is worrying but not enough to explain 120ms idle gap. Did we see any CPU GC / runtime-level stall?

maria: Checked GC logs for runtime: there are periodic KV cache eviction sweeps at the same timestamps. When the runtime triggers a cache compaction it pauses async prefetch workers briefly (~30-60ms) while reclaiming pinned pages. That, combined with memcpy backpressure, could amplify to ~120ms.

sophie: Wait — the new batching window increases per-request batching delay on the gateway side. So gateway intentionally waits up to 3ms to form batches, but that shouldn't make 100ms. However, if the runtime is doing synchronous KV compaction and holding off processing new incoming RPCs (thread pool saturation), the gateway's TCP buffers could fill and then sends will block until kernel/memcpy frees up PCIe bandwidth => visible in perfetto as a gap.

leo: That matches the chain: (batching wait) -> (gateway attempts send) -> (runtime prefetch + KV compaction) -> (memcpy backlog) -> (kernel launch) -> (proc). So end-to-end tail = sum of these.

maria: Reproducer command I'm using locally:
```
# capture a problematic window
BATCH_WINDOW_MS=3 make run-loadtest && sudo nsys profile --output=out1845 --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt ./bin/runtime --loadtest
# then open in perfetto
python tools/upload_trace.py out1845.qdrep s3://redwood-samples/nsys/
```

zhang: Can you also try with BATCH_WINDOW_MS=1 and disable KV compaction (set KV_EAGER_COMPACT=0) to see which factor dominates?

maria: Yes. I ran a quick A/B last hour:
- baseline (window=3, compaction=on): p95 spike present, 95p->~120ms extra
- window=1, compaction=on: spike smaller but still present (~70ms)
- window=1, compaction=off: almost gone (tail down to ~15-25ms).
So compaction looks like the main catalyzer.

sophie: Interesting. The compaction was meant to reduce long-term memory but we probably need to make it async/non-blocking or do rate-limited sweeps.

leo: For immediate mitigation: revert batching window to 1ms in gateway (short-term) and flip KV_EAGER_COMPACT=0 on the runtime fleet for the next hour, while we implement non-blocking compaction. Can ops roll that out to the affected pool?

infra-bot: roll request noted. ops-runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-compaction-tuning
rollout command: opsctl apply --pool=prod-runtime --set KV_EAGER_COMPACT=0 --reason="temp mitigation for tail spikes"

zhang: Long-term fixes: 1) make compaction incremental (yield to async prefetch work), 2) add backpressure metrics to gateway for socket send-block time, 3) add a perf-test that exercises high-prefetch with variable batch windows and asserts 95p < 50ms

maria: I can open the PR for non-blocking compaction and a perf regression test next week. For now I've queued the ops rollback and kicked off nsys captures with the BATCH_WINDOW_MS=1 experiments.

sophie: Thanks. Good find. Leaving a small note for QA: watch for memory drift if we disable eager compaction for long. :pray:

leo: Great thread. If anyone has additional perfetto slices that look different (e.g., no memcpy but long syscall delays), paste them here. Otherwise I'll start the compaction PR review tomorrow.

maria: Will post the nsys qdrep links once uploads finish. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
